BiblicalUsage: Kamelos is the camel — the beast of the desert, the garment of the Baptist, and the measure of the impossible. John wore raiment of camel's hair; and Jesus says it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the camel is there to make the impossible plain: no man can thread himself through the needle's eye, and that is exactly why the rich man — and I — need God to do what is impossible with men. With men it is impossible, but with God all things are possible.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
